# Canonical stop/restart success — implemented source confirmation

`service.stop` and `service.restart` may report `succeeded` only after the OLD OWNED INVOCATION is proven settled. Readiness alone is never this proof. Receipt fields and endpoints are unchanged.

The action adapter captures the pre-dispatch canonical owner identity under the existing lifecycle lease/CAS checks. After delegated text Manager stop/restart, it verifies settlement before releasing that lease. After delegated image systemd jobs, it independently observes the image native owner and asks `CanonicalIdentityReader.old_owner_settled` about the captured OLD immutable container identity, even when the currently selected replacement is healthy.

The independent reader proves the old exact container absent through a successful bounded fixed-ID Docker inventory; or proves it stopped with `Running=false` and PID0; or proves a restarted same container has both a different nonzero main PID and different StartedAt. A replacement container being ready cannot hide an old live container. When the previous canonical owner was absent, restart captures successful fixed registered-name absence under the canonical lease immediately before dispatch. That internal proof remains valid when the new owner later occupies the name; contradictory/nonempty names refuse dispatch. Missing metadata alone is insufficient.

Stop success additionally requires the current owned workload stopped (PID0 if an owned container remains). Image stop requires both fixed image units inactive and the native backend itself not running. Image restart requires a running ready replacement, independent old-owner settlement, changed PID/StartedAt when reusing an ID, and a different native owner run_id. An API-unit restart or HTTP readiness response alone cannot produce success. Control stop requires its fixed unit inactive, no pending job and MainPID0; restart requires a changed InvocationID and changed/nonzero MainPID.

Unknown, malformed, contradictory or still-live-old-owner evidence fails the operation (or remains unknown/interrupted after an interrupted journal write). It never emits succeeded and never replays the old request. Fresh readiness after canonical success can admit NEW work; consumers may clear uncertain request quarantine only for the matching confirmed stop/restart operation, never for `service.start`, readiness alone, or stale CAS.

Verification: `python3 tests/test_node_action_owner.py -q` passes34 tests and `python3 tests/test_node_actions.py -q` passes11. Fixtures include actual Manager stop/restart with the real canonical lease and controlled Docker/storage, unchanged peers, failed preflight before stop, image replacement readiness while the old backend remains live, unchanged native PID/start/run_id rejection, successful proved replacement, and control PID0 settlement. These are source/offline fixtures, not live VM lifecycle acceptance. Root owns the independently implemented filtered Docker old-owner reader and its tests.

Also corrected the image inherited-latch validation boot adapter: node collector `boot_age_seconds` maps explicitly to HardwarePolicy `uptime_seconds`; fixture verifies150.25 seconds maps unchanged. Inherited-latch clearing retains journal-before-write and failed stale_state refresh semantics.
